title: A New View of the World: UN Votes for More Accurate Map
subtitle: The United Nations has officially moved to adopt a new world map that better represents the true size of Africa.

summary.en: The United Nations General Assembly recently voted to replace the traditional Mercator map with the Equal Earth projection. This decision follows a long campaign led by Togo to show Africa's true size. While 164 nations supported the change, the United States voted against it. Supporters believe the new map promotes fairness and truth in how we see the world. Critics argue that the UN should focus on more urgent international issues instead of historical map designs.
summary.zh: 聯合國大會近期投票決定，以「等積地球投影法」取代傳統的麥卡托地圖。此項決策源於多哥所領導的一項長期運動，旨在呈現非洲的真實大小。儘管有一百六十四個國家支持這項變革，美國仍投下反對票。支持者認為新地圖能促進我們看待世界時的公平與真實性。批評者則主張，聯合國應專注於更迫切的國際議題，而非歷史性的地圖設計。

paragraphs.en: The United Nations General Assembly has officially voted to move away from the traditional world map that has been used for hundreds of years. In a major decision, 164 nations supported a resolution to adopt the 'Equal Earth' projection. This new map is designed to show the true size of continents, specifically correcting the way Africa is represented. This vote is the latest step in a long campaign to change how the world is viewed, following earlier reports that the traditional map was misleading.
paragraphs.zh: 聯合國大會已正式投票決定，將捨棄沿用數百年的傳統世界地圖。在一項重大決策中，有一百六十四個國家支持採用「等積地球投影法」（Equal Earth projection）的決議。這款新地圖旨在呈現各大洲的真實大小，特別是修正了非洲在過往地圖中的呈現方式。此次投票是長期以來推動改變世界觀運動的最新進展，此前已有報導指出傳統地圖具有誤導性。

paragraphs.en: For centuries, the world has relied on the Mercator map, created in 1569 by a cartographer named Gerardus Mercator. According to BBC News, this map was originally designed to help European explorers travel by sea. Because it is difficult to show a round globe on a flat piece of paper, the map had to make compromises. As a result, countries near the top and bottom of the Earth appear much larger than they really are, while countries near the equator appear smaller. This has led to a major misunderstanding of geography: on the Mercator map, Africa looks similar in size to Greenland, even though Africa is actually 14 times larger.
paragraphs.zh: 數百年來，世界一直依賴由製圖師傑拉杜斯·麥卡托（Gerardus Mercator）於一五六九年所創的麥卡托投影地圖。根據英國廣播公司新聞（BBC News）報導，這款地圖最初是為了協助歐洲探險家進行海上航行而設計。由於要在平面的紙張上呈現圓形的地球相當困難，該地圖不得不做出妥協。結果導致地球頂端與底部的國家看起來比實際大得多，而赤道附近的國家則顯得較小。這造成了嚴重的地理認知偏差：在麥卡托地圖上，非洲看起來與格陵蘭島大小相近，但實際上非洲的面積是格陵蘭島的十四倍。

paragraphs.en: Supporters of the change argue that this is more than just a simple error. According to Deutsche Welle, Togolese Foreign Minister Robert Dussey told the UN that maps are never neutral. He explained that they shape our education, our imagination, and how we understand the place of different people in the world. By making Africa look smaller, the old map has, for a long time, downplayed the continent’s vast resources, population, and potential for investment. The online campaign group #CorrectTheMap noted that you could fit the United States, China, India, Japan, Mexico, and much of Europe into Africa and still have land left over.
paragraphs.zh: 支持這項變革的人士認為，這不僅僅是一個簡單的錯誤。根據德國之聲（Deutsche Welle）報導，多哥外交部長羅伯特·杜塞（Robert Dussey）向聯合國表示，地圖從來都不是中立的。他解釋說，地圖塑造了我們的教育、想像力，以及我們對不同族群在世界上所處位置的理解。透過將非洲縮小，舊地圖長期以來淡化了該大陸廣大的資源、人口以及投資潛力。網路運動組織「修正地圖」（#CorrectTheMap）指出，將美國、中國、印度、日本、墨西哥以及歐洲大部分地區放入非洲後，仍有剩餘空間。

paragraphs.en: France, which helped lead the resolution, has already announced that it will stop using the Mercator map in its official work. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot stated that while changing a map does not change the world itself, correcting a false image is an important act of truth. Togo has also shared plans to update the maps used in its schools by the end of this year. It is important to note that the UN vote is not legally binding. The UN clarified that the new map does not change how ships or planes navigate, as the Mercator projection remains useful for those specific purposes.
paragraphs.zh: 協助主導此項決議的法國已宣布，將停止在官方業務中使用麥卡托地圖。法國外交部長尚-諾埃爾·巴羅（Jean-Noël Barrot）表示，雖然更換地圖並不會改變世界本身，但修正錯誤的圖像是一種重要的求真行動。多哥也分享了計畫，將在今年年底前更新其學校使用的地圖。值得注意的是，聯合國的投票並不具備法律約束力。聯合國澄清，新地圖不會改變船隻或飛機的導航方式，因為麥卡托投影法在這些特定用途上仍然實用。

paragraphs.en: However, the decision was not supported by everyone. The United States was the only country to vote against the resolution. Yaryna Ferencevych, a US representative at the UN, argued that the project was a distraction from more serious global problems. According to Deutsche Welle, she stated that the UN should be focusing on international peace, prosperity, and good relations rather than debating map designs from the 16th century. She suggested that the move was part of an 'ideological agenda' rather than a practical necessity. Six other countries, including Ukraine and Serbia, chose to abstain, meaning they did not vote for or against the change.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，這項決定並未獲得所有人支持。美國是唯一投票反對該決議的國家。美國駐聯合國代表雅琳娜·費倫塞維奇（Yaryna Ferencevych）主張，這項計畫分散了對更嚴重全球問題的注意力。根據德國之聲報導，她表示聯合國應該專注於國際和平、繁榮與良好關係，而非爭論十六世紀的地圖設計。她認為此舉更像是「意識形態議程」，而非實際需求。包括烏克蘭與塞爾維亞在內的其他六個國家則選擇棄權，意即他們未對此變革投下贊成或反對票。

paragraphs.en: Despite the criticism, those behind the campaign see this as a victory for fairness. Lerato Mogoatlhe from the group Africa No Filter told the BBC that the misrepresentation of Africa on maps is a 'narrative issue' that has contributed to misinformation about the continent for a long time. For many, the adoption of the Equal Earth map is a way to ensure that future generations grow up with a more accurate understanding of our planet. As the world continues to change, this decision reflects a growing desire to ensure that global institutions represent all regions with greater accuracy and respect.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管面臨批評，推動此項運動的人士仍將其視為公平的勝利。來自「非洲無濾鏡」（Africa No Filter）組織的勒拉托·莫戈阿特勒（Lerato Mogoatlhe）告訴英國廣播公司，地圖上對非洲的錯誤呈現是一個「敘事問題」，長期以來助長了關於該大陸的錯誤資訊。對許多人而言，採用等積地球地圖是確保未來世代在成長過程中，能對我們的星球有更準確理解的一種方式。隨著世界持續變遷，這項決定反映出人們日益強烈的願望，即確保全球機構能以更高的準確度與尊重來呈現所有地區。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To stop using or doing something and start using or doing something else.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 不再使用或採取某種做法，轉而採用新方式。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個片語，字面上是「移開」，這裡指「放棄舊習慣或舊政策」。文中：The United Nations General Assembly has officially voted to move away from the traditional world map that has been used for hundreds of years.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To make something seem less important or valuable than it really is.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 輕描淡寫、貶低、使……顯得不重要。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於新聞報導，指刻意縮小某事物的影響力。文中：By making Africa look smaller, the old map has, for a long time, downplayed the continent’s vast resources, population, and potential for investment.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Having the legal power to force someone to do what has been agreed.
keyTerms.noteZh: 在法律語境中常用，容易被誤認為是 bind 的現在分詞（正在綁）。文中：It is important to note that the UN vote is not legally binding.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To choose not to use your vote in an election or a formal decision.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於政治與投票場合，指選擇不表態。文中：Six other countries, including Ukraine and Serbia, chose to abstain, meaning they did not vote for or against the change.

previousArticles.summaryEn: The United Nations General Assembly has voted to move away from the traditional Mercator map. This decision follows a campaign led by Togo to use the more accurate 'Equal Earth' projection. Supporters argue the old map makes Africa look much smaller than it really is. The United States was the only country to vote against the resolution, calling it a distraction. While the new map is not mandatory, it is expected to change how schools and organizations view the world.

quiz.question: According to the article, why is the Mercator map considered problematic in terms of how it depicts Africa?

options.A: It was designed by a cartographer who intentionally wanted to diminish the importance of African nations.
options.B: It makes Africa appear significantly smaller than it is in reality compared to countries near the poles.
options.C: It fails to show the accurate size of Greenland, which is actually 14 times larger than Africa.
options.D: It creates a false impression that Africa is the same size as the United States, China, and India combined.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第二段明確指出，由於麥卡托投影法為了將圓形地球展現在平面上，導致靠近赤道的國家（如非洲）看起來比實際小，而靠近兩極的國家看起來比實際大。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章未提及麥卡托有刻意貶低非洲的意圖，僅提到是為了航海用途。選項 C 顛倒了事實，文章提到的是非洲比格陵蘭大 14 倍，而非格陵蘭比非洲大。選項 D 雖然提到了這些國家，但文章是指這些國家『可以放進』非洲內，而非兩者大小相等。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the practical impact of the UN's recent vote?

options.A: It will immediately force all international shipping and aviation companies to update their navigation systems.
options.B: It serves primarily as a symbolic shift in representation rather than a change in functional navigation tools.
options.C: It will legally require all member nations to stop using the Mercator map in their school textbooks.
options.D: It is expected to resolve the primary political conflicts between the United States and other UN members.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據第四段，聯合國明確表示此投票並無法律約束力（not legally binding），且航海與航空導航仍會繼續使用麥卡托投影，這顯示該決議的意義在於象徵性的觀點轉變，而非技術層面的強制更換。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章說導航用途不受影響。選項 C 錯誤，因為投票無法律強制力。選項 D 錯誤，因為美國反對該決議是基於其認為這是「意識形態議程」，而非單純的航海導航問題，且該決議無法解決更廣泛的國際衝突。

quiz.question: In the third paragraph, what does the word 'neutral' mean in the context of Minister Robert Dussey's statement that 'maps are never neutral'?

options.B: Physically balanced on a flat surface

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在文中，Robert Dussey 指出地圖會塑造我們的教育與想像，暗示地圖帶有特定的觀點或偏見，因此「never neutral」意指地圖並非「不偏不倚、客觀中立」的。選項 B 是對該詞的字面誤解，與地圖的政治含義無關。選項 C 雖然地圖涉及測量，但原文重點在於地圖背後的隱含意義，而非測量精確度。選項 D 雖然接近中立的意思，但「不活躍」並不能精準描述地圖作為一種「傳達訊息的工具」所具備的性質。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding the adoption of the 'Equal Earth' projection?

options.A: The UN is replacing the Mercator map because it is no longer useful for modern sea navigation.
options.B: The United States is the only nation that understands the scientific flaws of the new map projection.
options.C: The shift represents a move toward correcting historical biases in how we visually represent the world's geography.
options.D: The 'Equal Earth' map will solve all global misinformation issues regarding the size of various continents.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文的核心在於探討為何聯合國支持採用新地圖，強調這是為了糾正長期以來麥卡托地圖對非洲等地區的誤導性呈現，並反映出一種對公平與準確性的追求。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到麥卡托地圖對航海仍有用。選項 B 錯誤，美國反對是因為認為這是「意識形態議程」，而非基於科學缺陷。選項 D 過於誇大，文章僅提到這是一個「敘事問題」，並未宣稱能解決所有全球錯誤資訊。
